post.caption: Black carbonado diamonds once tipped rock drills. Carbonado is a porous black clump of tiny diamond crystals. It is found only in Brazil and the Central African Republic, and long ago South America and Africa were joined. Some studies say it is about 3.8 billion years old. Scientists still debate how it formed, and one 2006 study suggested it may have come from space. Portuguese prospectors named it for its charcoal look. A Brazilian one weighing over 3,000 carats was cut up for drills. A cut carbonado of 555.55 carats sold at Sotheby's in 2022.
